utterances.text: What I would like to be clear about is whether, in your recollection, on the 15th of April, the HVO had access to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You could come up to the village, for example, on the 15th of April. The road was still clear in one way, but I don't know specifically what the situation was for every area. Whether there were checkpoints or not, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, I am much obliged. I realise that you are coming to the end of a very long period of testimony, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Shahabuddeen. Let me turn to Judge Rodrigues. Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. General Blaskic, I have three questions. The first will take us back to the questions I asked earlier this afternoon. You already said this afternoon that there were investigations into Vitez and Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And into the incident of the truck bomb.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that from the security service, I received information that it was the Vitezovi unit who was behind it and that I was informed that this information was sent on to the competent authorities at the head office in Mostar. I also required the commanders of the independent unit of the Vitezovi to conduct an investigation within the unit to uncover the perpetrator of that terrorist act, and I never received information from him as to who was behind it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. And as regards Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I recall, the civilian police took over from 14 -- 15.00 of the 8th, Grbavica, and they took over authority, blockades, security, investigation in the area. I remember, in relation to Grbavica, that it was on the 18th of September when I received congratulations from a major of UNPROFOR for overall cooperation and the understanding that I showed for protecting the civilians at Grbavica and the professional way in which it was conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Throughout the situation, when investigations were being carried out, did you ever see the results of the investigations? Did you never see them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the results were such as I spoke about. They were not ideal. They were not always like that, and unfortunately here in the courtroom, I saw intimations of the results and one result --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, General, for interrupting you, but I'm speaking about the final results. Because there are situations when you had preliminary information, and you weren't satisfied and you insisted on learning more, but I'm speaking about the definitive results, the definitive results of the investigations. Did you remember receive any results of those investigations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's what I had wanted to say, Your Honour. I did see them here in the courtroom, and it is the document by the head of the security service to the minister --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: At that time. At that time. I'm thinking about that time. At that time, did you actually have in your own hands the results of any of the investigations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not have them in the sense of discovering and identifying the perpetrators. I didn't have any results of that kind, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: My second question: You told us, throughout your testimony, that you went to Kiseljak, you left your wife and your life in Austria, in order to fight against the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: What were your reactions when you learned for sure that, in the end, you were not going to fight your enemies, the Serbs, but your allies, the Muslims? What were your reactions to that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honour, I believe for a long time that the basic enemy was the army of the Republika Srpska and that there were incidents and conflicts which we would succeed in overcoming. I believed deeply that regardless of what happened during the January conflict and regardless of the first stage of the April conflict, that we would be able to overcome this problem through a joint struggle up at the front line facing the Serbs and through joint commands and that those problems would be surmounted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: When you really believed that, in the end, you were going to fight with your allies, what was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I found myself in a situation, as I have already said, I was caught up in it. I was in a total encirclement, and even my assistants criticised me and said why I believed in a march and why I gave assistance to the BH army and why I helped and supported in communality and this joint effort, because I truly did believe that all the problems would be overcome. Ultimately, the Washington Agreement was fastest realised and implemented by the soldiers themselves, and the commander of the 3rd Corps told me on several occasions that the problem did not lie in the army but that the problem lay with politics, in the realm of politics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General. That's your answer. My third question: We are trying to reach some conclusions. You are perhaps familiar with all the theory of working together. There's always a first and then a second part, coalitions, I'm talking about. This afternoon, you said that the HVO was in front of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was stronger than the HVO. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the area that I found myself, and I still claim that there were at least 200.000 (sic) HVO soldiers for operative use at the operative disposal of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It says in the transcript that at least 200.000 HVO soldiers for operative use were at the operative disposal of the BH army. I'm not sure that that was what the witness wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If you permit me, Your Honour. General Blaskic, could you explain once again to us the proportions between the HVO and the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that we can be clear about things?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, the time we're discussing now, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had, within its operative use, 260.000 soldiers, of which number you must deduct soldiers who were in the Bihac pocket and soldiers who were in the Gorazde pocket and the other pockets, and perhaps it was 60.000 or 70.000 of those soldiers, which means that 200.000 soldiers were left of the BH army against the HVO. The HVO never had so many soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Following this idea, if you add the VRS, that is, the Serb army, what place, what rank would you put that army? You have the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the HVO, and if you were to set up a list by strength, where would you put the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Technically speaking, in first place, but technical means does not make up an army alone. The human factor, then we have the BH army in the first place in the sense of the most numerous; and the HVO would have its position there in the last place, would take last place, bottom place, because I think it was created as an organisational structure by those who did not have sufficient knowledge about how an army should be formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, let me go to the background. It is perfectly natural and I do understand that the HVO and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were allies fighting against the Serbian army, but what I don't understand is that when the HVO and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina began to fight one another, why the first army, that is the VRS, did not conquer the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, first I think that it took over more territory; had it had double the number of soldiers, it wouldn't have been able to control it. At one point, it had 75 per cent of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina under its control, and it found this suitable, to correspond to its desires, to have a lull for a time and to solve its economic problems by selling ammunition or trying to obtain enough fuel and to engage in trade of this kind while the allies were confronting each other. So what they did was to pacify themselves or solve their problems in eastern Bosnia. But, for the most part, they became passive, they pacified themselves in our area, and even incited the conflict because this corresponded to their ends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Thank you for helping me to understand things well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. We are going to finish. I think we've got to reach the conclusion. I have a question which will have two smaller ones. I would like you to be very precise in your answer. Do you consider that there was a draft policy on the part of the HVO, starting in the fall of 1992, in terms of territory, in terms of administration, pedagogical or any other type of administration? Do you think that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in the sense of some ideas, I do believe that there was some kind of political project which was the consequence of the chaos and the overall situation in which each peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina found itself at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Did you make a distinction between the political options of the HVO and your own military operations? That's my second question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw myself as a military commander. Of course, I made a distinction between political options and military options, and I never considered that I ought to be a politician within the HVO. The HVO policy was led by those given the mandate by the Croatian people from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: At any point, through your presence or through demonstrations or through meetings, did you ever think that you were participating in the HVO's political options?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I attended only two, possibly three meetings. I have already said, at the first one I was introduced as a guest and the new commander, and at the second one, I submitted a report on the military situation. I did not take part in political decision-making nor did I have any political function to perform whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Going back to the question asked by Judge Rodrigues. When the conflict changed in terms of its nature and its combatants, did you say to your chiefs that "I do not want to participate in the HVO's political options"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not consider that I ever participated in the political options of the HVO, Mr. President, and I always saw myself, I personally, as a military commander, and I left politics to the political leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You were seen as a military commander and you always repeat that. But when the conflict, the reach of the conflict and the adversaries changed, the military options, that is, your military option, also had a change in nature, because the political nature of the HVO, of which we are not a part, decided -- or, at least, took a position in the conflict against the Muslims, no longer against the Serbs. Did you inform your supreme command that you were no longer part of the contract to which you had subscribed in respect of your chiefs? Did you do that at any point? Did you say it? Did you do it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the sense that I did not consider myself a military commander, I did not. But, Mr. President, in Central Bosnia, where I was the commander, the only policy was to survive. The situation was quite different in the southern regions, in Herzegovina, where the relationship between the army and the HVO was quite different. In my area, it was a question of survival alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Beyond survival, there was a political project on the part of the HVO -- you recognise that and you said that -- in which you were not involved. I understood that. But there was a political project on the part of the HVO. You acknowledge, at least, there was at least an embryonic form of that project. Did you inform your superiors that you would come to fight against the Serbs, that you were not going to continue to adhere to that political project? Did you do that? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not in a position to see the political project of the fight against the Bosniak Muslims, if we're just talking about a political project. I was caught up in Central Bosnia and the conflict there, and the only politics or policy was that of survival.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: My final question: Could we say that the attitude of being purely and entirely military, could you say that that caused you difficulties with your superiors?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know whether it created problems or not with my superiors and what problems they had, but I truly did advocate that position and the view that these conflicts would also be overcome through agreement and through building up a joint command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is my final question: How do you interpret the fact that you were, in fact, promoted, that you were recognised by the HVO hierarchy and then even later on by Croatia, if you did not adhere to the political project? How do you explain that? Could you give us, give the Judges a personal explanation at least?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, not only by the policies of the HVO but representatives of the BH Republic as well. I was a witness of a meeting at which myself and Mr. Rasim Delic were the representatives of the joint command of the army of the federation and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic was present there as the supreme commander, and he had no criticisms to make of a promotion of that kind, and I was the commander of the army of the federation together with Rasim Delic for almost a year, and I explained this by virtue of my military and professional capabilities and my professional conduct in performing my military duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
